title: King and pawn against king: predict the family
outcomes: Predicts win or draw for K+P v K positions that differ in side to move, king placement and pawn file
Changes one fact at a time and says whether the result flips
Recognises a change that leaves the result alone

steps.text: In **King and pawn against king: the king leads** the plan was king first, pawn only when needed. Now predict results in a family of positions where one fact changes at a time: who is to move, where the kings stand, which file the pawn is on. Check them in that order. It is a **rule of thumb**; the tablebase decides each case.

steps.caption: White to move. Both king moves in front of the pawn win. The push e6 only draws.

line.say: Only now does the pawn advance, with the king beside it.
The pawn reaches e7, defended by the king on f6.
White's king steps to f7, guarding e8 and the pawn.
Now the pawn queens, guarded by the king.

claims.statement: White wins from the start position.
The push e6 does not win.

steps.text: Three facts change the answer in this lesson. The side to move: one tempo turns a win into a draw. The king positions relative to the pawn. The file: an edge-file pawn lets the defender run for the corner. How far the pawn has gone changes which squares the king needs, so rank can flip a result too; this lesson changes the other three facts. A change that leaves the result alone is as worth noticing as one that flips it.

steps.title: One tempo
steps.prompt: In the first position Black to move wins. Predict the second, where White is to move instead, and the third, where only the White king stands one file over.

steps.title: Centre file or edge file
steps.prompt: In the first position White wins. Predict the second, which is the same placement one file to the left, and the third, where only the Black king has moved.
Before each prediction: did you note the side to move first, then the kings, then the file? Which fact flipped a result you expected to hold?
